title: Fractional numeric filter values must be compared exactly, never truncated with int()
answers: Why does a filter like start_time = 1.5 match a run with start_time 1?
Do numeric search comparisons in the in-memory matcher truncate decimal values?
How should fractional values in numeric attribute filters be compared?
body:
Invariant: Numeric attribute comparisons keep fractional values exact. Do not call `int(value)` on an already-parsed float in the in-memory matchers.
Enforced in: mlflow/utils/search_utils.py:_does_run_match_clause, _does_model_match_clause, and _does_logged_model_match_clause, which only convert `value` when `isinstance(value, str)`.
What breaks if skipped: A filter such as `start_time = 1.5` silently becomes `start_time = 1` in the file store, so a run at 1 matches when it should not. The SQL run path (_get_sqlalchemy_filter_clauses) passes the float to SQLAlchemy, which binds it as FLOAT, so the two paths would disagree.
Constraints: Applies to run, model, and logged-model matchers. Experiments and evaluation datasets are excluded and must reject fractions (see the experiment/dataset guard note).
applies: In-memory numeric attribute matching for run, model and logged-model search in SearchUtils and its subclasses.
says: Filtering experiment runs by decimal start time matches runs with whole number timestamps.
Search results on the runs table include mismatched items due to decimal truncation.
Numeric attribute filters in run search should match exact decimal values without rounding.
Filtering logged models by fractional numbers unexpectedly matches models with truncated values.
Searching runs with decimal attribute values should not match runs with rounded integers.
search: In-memory numeric attribute comparisons for run, model, and logged-model search must preserve exact fractional values rather than truncating parsed floats with int(). In mlflow/utils/search_utils.py:_does_run_match_clause, _does_model_match_clause, and _does_logged_model_match_clause, conversion to integer only occurs when isinstance(value, str). Skipping exact comparison causes file store filters like start_time = 1.5 to match start_time 1, disagreeing with the SQL store where _get_sqlalchemy_filter_clauses binds floats directly. This rule applies to SearchUtils in-memory matchers for runs, models, and logged models, but excludes experiments and evaluation datasets, which reject fractions.
